name: Hotel Iravati Restaurant (Chowgan Restaurant)
why_it_matters: HPTDC's flagship Chamba property — the dining hall sits on the edge of the Chowgan with the bus stand and Lakshmi Narayan temple steps away. The kitchen is one of the few in town that will plate Chamba madra and chasnidar to order, and is the official tourist-board recommendation for traditional Himachali fare.
insider_tip: Pre-order the madra and chasnidar at least 2-3 hours ahead — the menu lists them but the kitchen prepares them only on request. Open 7:30 AM to 9:30 PM.
signature_address: Hotel Iravati (HPTDC), near Bus Stand & Laxmi Narayan Temple, Chamba 176310

name: Cafe Ravi View
why_it_matters: HPTDC-run wooden hut perched above the Ravi at the edge of the Chowgan — currently #2 of Chamba's TripAdvisor restaurants. The food is honest tourist-canteen fare; the reason to come is the 360-degree balcony view of the river meeting the town.
insider_tip: Sit on the outdoor deck, not inside. Avoid late-afternoon crowds in May-June; the view is best at golden hour after temple aarti at Lakshmi Narayan.

name: Mame da Dhaba
why_it_matters: The local consensus pick for authentic Chambyali dham — the marriage-feast platter of madra, mash, khatta and rice that no tourist menu in town serves at this honesty. Sultanpur is a 5-minute drive across the river from Chowgan; the dhaba is a workers' kitchen, not a curated experience.
insider_tip: Dham is served at lunch only — turn up by 1 PM or the leaf-plates run out. Eat with your hand from the patal; spoons are an apology, not a service.
signature_address: Sultanpur, Chamba 176310 (5 min from Chowgan, across Ravi bridge)

name: Jagan Cafe
why_it_matters: Tucked off Museum Road near the Bhuri Singh Museum — the rare in-town spot that serves rajma madra without 4-hour pre-order. Small, slow, but the kitchen is honest and the window catches a sliver of Mani Mahesh on clear days.
insider_tip: Service is leisurely; don't sit down here on a tight bus-stand schedule. Pair it with a Bhuri Singh Museum visit — the museum and cafe are 200m apart.
signature_address: Museum Road, near Bhuri Singh Museum, Chamba 176310

name: Park View Restaurant
why_it_matters: A long-running family restaurant on the Court Road / Museum Road axis — described locally as one of Chamba's oldest sit-down eateries. The menu is north-Indian-meets-Indian-Chinese; reliable rather than ambitious, which is what you want after a 2-hour bus from Dalhousie.
insider_tip: Stick to the Indian side of the menu — the kitchen does jeera rice and chicken curry better than its hakka noodles.
signature_address: Court Road / Museum Road, main market, Chamba 176310

name: Hotel City Heart Restaurant
why_it_matters: Mid-range hotel restaurant in the main market near Champavati temple — one of the few central Chamba kitchens that serves rajma madra and a Chamba-style chicken curry from the regular menu rather than on pre-order. Reviewers consistently flag both as the dishes to order.
insider_tip: It's a hotel restaurant with hotel-restaurant pricing — order the local dishes (madra, chamba chicken), skip the pizza-and-pasta side of the menu.
signature_address: Court Road, near Champavati Temple, Chamba 176310

name: Hotel Champak Restaurant (HPTDC)
why_it_matters: Second HPTDC property in Chamba — sits on the slope above Chowgan in Mohalla Sapri with the broadest view of the maidan. The restaurant is plainer and quieter than Iravati's, which is the point if you want a no-fuss thali break between the museum and the Lakshmi Narayan temple.
insider_tip: Better for breakfast and tea-stop than dinner; the Iravati kitchen does the local dishes more reliably. Walk down to Chowgan after — the view from the property is the bonus.
signature_address: The Champak (HPTDC), Mohalla Sapri, overlooking Chowgan, Chamba 176310

name: Downtown Restaurant and Banquets
why_it_matters: Currently TripAdvisor's #1 Chamba restaurant — a newer banquet-style multi-cuisine kitchen on the Sach Pass highway near Bhadram zero point. Not where you go for Chamba madra; where you go when the family wants air-con, biryani, and a barbecue platter.
insider_tip: Open 11 AM-11 PM, free parking — useful if you're driving in from Dalhousie or Khajjiar and want a non-hotel dinner. Reservations help on weekends.
signature_address: Near Bhadram Zero Point, Sach Pass Highway, Chamba 176310
